transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve been losing a lot of time checking things, I guess. Re-reading emails and texts, opening folders again, replaying conversations in my head before I can leave the house or start working. It’s like I’m trying to make sure I didn’t miss some serious mistake.
Do you feel anxious when you're checking these things or replaying conversations in your head?

Yes… anxious, I guess. It’s mostly this feeling that if I don’t check again, I might’ve missed something important—like a serious mistake in an email or a folder or something I said. So I re-read or replay it until I feel a little more sure, but it takes a lot of time.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind even when you try to ignore them?

Yeah… there are thoughts that keep coming back. Like when I’m trying to focus on a system design or prepare a lesson, I’ll suddenly think maybe I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or mishandled some family photos, or let someone down in the community. I know I’ve already gone over it, but it sort of barges in anyway, and I have trouble just letting it pass.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks or repetitions in a specific way or a certain number of times?

Not really a set number, no. It’s more like… I have to keep re-reading the email or reopening the folder until it feels like I can prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake. Same with replaying a conversation before I leave or start work. It just eats up time.
Are you trying to prevent something bad or unpleasant from happening when you repeat these checks or replay conversations?

Yeah… I think so. It’s like I’m trying to stop some mistake from catching up with me later—an email I read wrong, a folder I didn’t check, something I said that came out badly. I keep going over it until I can sort of prove to myself it’s okay… though it doesn’t always last.
Do you feel like these repetitions or checks help reduce your anxiety or unease in any way?

Yeah… for a little while, I guess. If I re-read the email or reopen the folder, I feel less uneasy, like I’ve proved I didn’t mess something up. But then it can come back, and I lose more time doing it again.
Do you feel like there's something that needs to be 'just right' when you're checking things or replaying conversations?

Sort of. It’s not “just right” like a pattern, exactly. It’s more like I don’t feel done until I’ve checked the email or the folder enough that I’m convinced I didn’t make a mistake. Same with replaying a conversation… I keep going until it feels settled, I guess.
Do you feel like your checking or replaying is driven more by the fear of making a mistake, or by a feeling that things need to be in a certain order or balanced?

More the mistake thing. I don’t really care if things are balanced or in some order. It’s more… I keep re-reading emails or texts, reopening folders, going back over conversations, because I’m trying to convince myself I didn’t miss something serious. It just takes up time.
Are these habits of checking and replaying conversations interfering with your work, relationships, or daily life in a significant way?

Yeah… I’d say it has. Work is slower than it should be. I’ve missed some design milestones, and I’ve had to push back mentoring sessions I used to be pretty reliable about.

And, um… there was a youth coding workshop I cared about, and I ended up late and not really prepared. That was embarrassing.
How much distress do these habits of checking and replaying conversations cause you?

It’s… pretty upsetting, yeah. Mostly because I can see the time disappearing. I’ll be re-reading an email or going back through texts, or opening the same folder again, and it feels like I’m trying to prove I didn’t make some serious mistake. It’s frustrating more than anything.
Are these habits affecting your relationships with family or friends in any way?

A bit, I guess. Not in a big dramatic way, but when work slows down and I miss design milestones, it spills over. I’ve had to postpone mentoring sessions I used to be reliable about.

And there was a youth coding workshop I cared about… I was late and not really prepared. That was embarrassing.
Are there any situations or activities that you avoid because of your need to check or replay things?
I’m not sure I’d call it avoiding, exactly. I haven’t really noticed specific things I stay away from because of it… it’s more that some things just take me longer than they should.
Do you have any other repetitive behaviors or mental acts that you feel driven to perform, aside from checking and replaying conversations?

Mostly the same kind of thing, I think. Re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders… and the mental part, replaying conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work. It’s like I’m trying to make sure I didn’t miss something or make a serious mistake.
Do you feel like these habits are affecting your overall well-being or ability to function in daily life?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not like everything has fallen apart, but my work has definitely slowed down. I’ve missed some design milestones, and I’ve had to push back mentoring sessions I used to be pretty dependable with.

And… I was late and not really prepared for a youth coding workshop I cared about. That was hard to sit with. Embarrassing, mostly.

Are there other areas of your life, aside from work and the examples you've mentioned, where you feel like these habits are causing problems or making it hard for you to do things you want or need to do?

Not really beyond that… or at least nothing that stands out. It’s mainly work getting slower, missing some design milestones, and having to move mentoring sessions I used to keep up with pretty reliably.

The workshop thing too — being late and not prepared for it. That bothered me. I felt pretty embarrassed.
Are you feeling like your relationships with friends or family are suffering because of the distress these habits cause you?

Not so much friends or family, no. I mean… the main place I notice it is work. Things take longer, I’ve missed design milestones, postponed mentoring sessions I used to handle fine.

And that coding workshop… being late and not really prepared, that was embarrassing. But relationships specifically, I don’t think that’s been the main problem.
Are there any other areas of your life where you feel like these habits are making it hard for you to function or causing you significant distress?

Mostly the same things, I guess. Work has slowed down enough that I’ve missed some design milestones, and I’ve had to postpone mentoring sessions I used to be pretty reliable about.

And… that youth coding workshop. I was late and not really prepared, and that bothered me. I felt embarrassed. Other than that, I’m not sure there’s much else.
Are there any activities or situations that you're avoiding altogether because of the anxiety or distress caused by your need to check or replay things?
I don’t think I’m avoiding things altogether, no. It’s more that some things take longer or I put them off a bit, but I can’t think of anything I’ve completely stopped doing because of it.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but have given up because of the time spent checking or replaying things?

I haven’t really given anything up completely, no. It’s more… work has taken the hit. I’ve missed some design milestones, postponed mentoring sessions I used to keep up with.

And there was a youth coding workshop I cared about—I showed up late and not very prepared. That was… embarrassing.
